text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crude oil exports earn Nigeria $1.1 billion in September and October this year, petroleum ministry sources say.
- Court orders state oil company NNPC to insure its assets with state insurer NICON and not with private firms.
- Government watchdog on economy lists refurbishing of oil refineries, fertiliser plants, steel and machine tools mills as projects that should get priority in 1997 to benefit common man.
- U.S. ambassador says safety of Americans was sole reason for warning about a danger of bomb blasts at Nigerian airports in last two weeks of December; Nigeria says the U.S. statement was offensive.

- Commonwealth Secretary-General Emeka Anyaoku, a Nigerian, says in New Year statement from London that Commonwealth is still concerned about Nigeria one year after it was suspended from the group for hanging nine minority rights activists.
- Central bank mops up 700 million naira from circulation through sale of treasury bills at the weekend.
- Despite end of year lull, stock exchange traded 2.1 million shares worth 16 million naira on Monday.
- Unviable government parastatals or agencies will either be scrapped or merged with others next year, officials say.
